Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: flat albedo texture atlas for 3D liquor bottle labels, not a picture of bottles
Primary request: exactly sixteen DIFFERENT photographed paper liquor labels with corresponding neck-label strips, arranged in an EXACT equal 4-column by 4-row grid, 16 square cells, row-major reading order. Each cell must be entirely independent and different from all other cells and other sheets. Early 2000s home tiki bar commercial spirits shelf appearance.
Input images: Image 1 is a shelf reference for label colors, layouts and printed texture. Image 2 is a supporting shelf reference for visual variation. Do not reconstruct the scenes.
Composition/framing: perfectly square 2k atlas, flat orthographic front-facing scans with no perspective. Every square cell has a body-label rectangle filling local x=0.0625 to 0.9375, y=0.22 to 0.94, and one corresponding long thin neck-label strip local x=0.125 to 0.875, y=0.06 to 0.16. Pale neutral unprinted paper fills the small unused gaps. Do not draw grid lines or cell numbers.
Materials/textures: photographed printed paper albedo, fine fiber grain, subtle handling wear and faded fine print, commercial spot-color inks, crisp medium typography but naturally slightly imperfect archival paper quality. No peeled corners, no shadows. For black label cells, use black paper and aged white or gold ink; for cream labels use cream paper.
Text policy: reference brand typography is visual inspiration only; brands are unreadable in most shelf photos. Do NOT invent readable brand names, dates, alcohol percentages, age statements, awards, slogans or geographical claims. Dense tiny faded microprint may be genuinely indistinct. Use unique typographic letter-shapes and printer ornaments rather than invented legible claims. Only explicitly specified exact text is allowed. Give the main label a strongly visible category title in each cell, with DIFFERENT commercial font families, widths, weights and placements. Supporting microprint remains indistinct.
Lighting/mood: absolutely even neutral scan illumination; albedo only, no directional light, no glare, no gradients caused by lighting, no bottle form shading.
Constraints: 16 body labels and 16 matching neck strips, neither omitted nor duplicated. The 16 designs must differ in base color, type hierarchy, borders, emblems and edge framing. Do not show bottle illustrations, silhouettes, glass, caps, liquid, wood, shelf or surrounding objects. Do not repeat the same cream/red design. Keep all content strictly inside its assigned equal-size cell.
Aspect ratio: 1:1
